title: Physical argument hoisting makes constrained virtual operands unallocatable
summary: The two-address pass can extend a physical argument definition across an operand whose entire allocatable class overlaps it. Spilling cannot create an available register. This record migrates the existing September report and patch 0029; it is not a new discovery.

prior_work.source_assessment: Existing 0029 supplies the guard; it is separate from carry scheduling and far-pointer ABI exhaustion. Destination 0f031168a7cc retains the physical-copy hoist and lacks the guard. Its entry gate and caller require LiveIntervals; upstream removed LiveVariables support.
prior_work.binary_assessment: A privately rebuilt unpatched current-base llc is retained at build/0029-20261010/baseline/bin/llc. It reproduces the original IR failure at O1/O2/O3 and the LiveIntervals ordering failure. Historical September binaries/results remain dated evidence.
prior_work.decision: First structured migration of the September causal defect, not a duplicate discovery. Current-base matching-input IR/MIR red/green and the MOS suites establish the existing guard on the refreshed standalone branch; September evidence retains its original scope.

baseline.failure_signature: ran out of registers during register allocation in function 'stage'

historical_scope: September 16 discovery and September 22 repair/review remain recorded in the original report and linked validation. The current refresh records a new exact-base baseline without replacing the earlier inputs, binary identities or full cross-target evidence.

resolution.causal_explanation: The guard refuses hoisting physical definitions when all unreserved registers of a crossed virtual operand class overlap those definitions. This preserves a legal assignment at the crossed instruction; spilling cannot create another physical register. Classes with a spare member still permit the move.
resolution.trigger_check: The exact retained IR fails at O1/O2/O3 without the guard and passes with it. LiveIntervals ordering and allocation of that output fail for accumulator_argument and intervening_index before the guard; both pass afterward, while the spare-register move stays allowed. Current MOS CodeGen/MC: 140 passed, one unsupported, zero failures, Release assertions OFF. Current C matrix: 24 full-driver and 24 candidate-backend passes; identical emitted IR fails on the preserved unpatched backend in all 20 optimized runs and passes four O0 runs. The frontend is shared and unchanged by the backend patch, not a separately rebuilt pristine baseline Clang driver.
